slides.heading: Minimum Passes Of Matrix
slides.subtitle: AlgoExpert · Medium · Graphs
slides.narration: Let's solve Minimum Passes Of Matrix, a medium graphs problem. We'll restate the problem, build the intuition, walk through the approach, read the Java solution, and finish with its complexity.

slides.heading: The problem
bullets: Each pass, every negative adjacent to a positive flips sign.
Return the number of passes to clear all negatives, or -1 if impossible.
slides.narration: Here's the problem. Each pass, every negative adjacent to a positive flips sign. Return the number of passes to clear all negatives, or -1 if impossible. Multi-source BFS by levels.

slides.heading: Intuition
bullets: Multi-source BFS: each pass, positives flip their negative neighbours.
slides.narration: Multi-source BFS: each pass, positives flip their negative neighbours.

slides.heading: Brute force vs optimal
bullets: Simulate passes by rescanning the whole matrix → O((w·h)²)
Multi-source BFS: one level per pass → O(w·h)
slides.narration: Simulating each pass by rescanning the whole matrix can be quadratic in the number of cells. Multi-source breadth-first search starts from all positives at once, and each BFS level is exactly one pass.

slides.heading: Approach
bullets: 3. Flip negative neighbours and enqueue them
4. If negatives remain, return minus one
slides.narration: Step by step. First, queue all positives. Second, process one level per pass. Third, flip negative neighbours and enqueue them. Fourth, if negatives remain, return minus one.

slides.heading: Java solution
slides.narration: We enqueue all positive cells. Each round processes the current queue size, flips negative neighbours and enqueues them, and counts the pass if anything flipped. At the end, any remaining negative means minus one.

slides.heading: Complexity
slides.narration: Time is O of w times h. Space is O of w times h.

slides.heading: Edge cases & pitfalls
bullets: Only count passes that flip something
slides.narration: If some negatives are surrounded by zeros, return minus one. With no negatives, the answer is zero, so only count passes that flip something.

slides.heading: Interview tips & follow-ups
slides.narration: This is the rotting oranges pattern. Explain that BFS levels correspond exactly to passes.
